text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Dedicated pool 'leonix-prod-pool' GPU node gpu-12 reported repeated ECC counter spikes and NVLINK errors. Severity: high. Auto-eviction attempted: failed. Paginating on-call.
marta: grabbing this — I'm on call. pulling logs now.
chong: seeing same in telemetry — ECC corrected errors jumping, temp stable but errors correlate with small OOMs on long-running workloads.
sam: @marta @chong timeline? customer leonix currently on reserved capacity in vpc-us-west2-a, ~12 hosts. Any immediate user impact?
marta: customer reports elevated 429s on long chat sessions and a single request timed out 202. Sampled traces show retries hitting same host.
nora: pinging runtime for quick health check: `curl -s http://gpu-12/health || true` returns 502 intermittently.
aj-eng: adding: nvlink logs show `NVLINK-AER: pcie link reset` and kernel logs with `GPU ECC corrected > 1000 within 10m`. This looks like a hardware-level instability, possibly firmware regression from last vendor patch.
oncall-bob: I'm nearby if you want handover. Do we need to page vendor?
marta: yes, paging vendor after immediate mitigations. First, isolate tenant traffic from that node, drain workloads if safe. Plan: warm-drain node (evict new sessions, finish in-flight KV prefixes), then cold-drain and replace.
chong: warming drain command prepared:```bash
# mark node unschedulable for new allocations
redwoodctl node cordon gpu-12
# set routing weight to 0 for dedpool route
redwoodctl route set-weight leonix-prod-pool gpu-12 0
```
sam: want to avoid abrupt evictions for long chat sessions. Use `--grace-duration` 300s for in-flight flows.
aj-eng: agree. We'll enable prefix caching to allow resumed sessions to hit other hosts. Also enabling aggressive batching fallback on route for next 20m.
incident-bot: NOTE: Automated fallback enabled for leonix-prod-pool -> fallback model variant small-latency-quantized. Latency SLOs may change.
marta: executing warm-drain now. Starting with `cordon` and route weight 0. I'll monitor for queue build-up.
chong: logs after cordon: `worker_queue_backpressure: +12%` — traffic being routed away. No further ECC spikes in last 30s but still present historically.
oncall-bob: vendor page requested (Case #VND-9921). They acknowledged possible firmware corner-case on NVLINK error handling. ETA for firmware review 4 hours.
sam: customer ops (leonix-ops) messaged asking for impact summary. Drafting: "We've isolated a single GPU host in your dedicated pool due to hardware error; most traffic is routed away, minor elevated latencies for long sessions, no token leakage, full mitigation in progress"
aj-eng: preparing replacement host image and scheduling `recreate-node` job. Will attempt live firmware rollback only if vendor confirms safe.
nora: running quick queries to list affected tenants on gpu-12: only leonix workloads pinned there due to dedicated pool allocation. Good: tenant isolation confirmed.
marta: next step: cold-drain (evict remaining sessions) in 5m if no successful stable window. Will send 5-minute warning to #leonix-ops.
chong: also seeing occasional PCIe AER messages — could be stress-triggered. We'll check power and thermal telemetry; already within normal thresholds.
incident-bot: REMINDER: On-call handoff window in 45m. @oncall-bob please confirm if you want to take primary after warmdrain completes.
oncall-bob: happy to take over the incident after the drain finishes. Stand by.
marta: 5m warning sent to customer: "We will cold-drain gpu-12 in 5m to safely migrate sessions; expect small service blips for active long-lived connections"
sam: after cold-drain, plan is replace node (reimage + kernel downgrade) then run soak for 30m before rejoining dedpool. If vendor provides firmware hotfix sooner, might try patch & test.
aj-eng: created job `recreate/gpu-12-replace-218050` — will run once drain reaches 0 connections.
chong: drain progress: 57% -> 82% -> 100% over 14m. No unexpected evictions.
marta: cold-drain complete. Evictions: 23 sessions. No retries failed. Routing stable to fallback variants.
oncall-bob: taking primary now. I'll track vendor updates and coordinate replacement.
incident-bot: CUSTOMER IMPACT: leonix: elevated latencies for ~18 minutes during migration; some in-flight sessions experienced short reconnects. Severity recorded: degraded but contained to dedicated pool.
sam: logging follow-up action items: 1) Vendor firmware follow-up (Case VND-9921) 2) Replace gpu-12 with fresh host image + kernel 5.15 rollback 3) Add NVLINK ECC counter alert threshold tuning 4) Postmortem in 48h.
nora: capturing debug bundle: `/var/log/redwood/dumps/gpu-12-2180505432.tgz` uploaded to secure bucket.
aj-eng: proceeding with node replacement now. Kickoff `recreate` -> monitoring.
oncall-bob: vendor replied: preliminary root cause likely firmware handling of persistent corrected ECC under low thermal variance. They suggested firmware rollback as stopgap. Requested logs.
marta: will circle back to customer with timeline: nodereplace in progress, expect node back in pool in ~40-60 minutes.
incident-bot: STATUS: node gpu-12 removed from pool at 2180505920. Replacement host created at 2180506025. Health checks passing.
chong: new host passed `NVLINK self-test` and `ECC baseline` checks. No anomalies so far.
sam: rejoin the pool with gradual weight increase: 0 -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 10 min.
aj-eng: reweight commands executed. Monitoring traces for errors.
marta: all clear from leonix: "we saw a blip but throughput back to normal, thanks".
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: gpu-12 hardware issue mitigated via warm+cold drain, node replacement, tenant isolation. Postmortem assigned to @sam and @aj-eng.
chong: quick note for postmortem: consider adding automatic warm-drain policy for ECC spike > 500 in 10m for dedicated pools.
sam: noted. I'll put together timeline and RCA draft.
aj-eng: uploading config diffs and job logs to the PM ticket.
oncall-bob: great run team. Logging incident and closing channel after postmortem creation. :thumbsup:
